title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary stage) on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes). The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; downstream validation and the permitted single repair call (guarded arm only) were the only mechanisms for paired outcome differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary inferential test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered secondary descriptive summary (paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI, 10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We present the exact McNemar result as the preregistered confirmatory outcome, present the bootstrap CI as a preregistered descriptive summary, explicitly label a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) as exploratory/post‑hoc (it was not specified in the frozen preregistration), and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, high baseline validity, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations promises reduced manual effort but raises safety risks: multi‑step sequencing errors, transient invariant violations, and protected‑field interference can convert plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior surveys and controlled studies document LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that affect code and configuration generation, motivating architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures [1],[2].

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) that isolates purely downstream validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Our precise research question is: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics), to what degree can a downstream deterministic validator plus a single allowed repair call (guarded pipeline with a canary stage) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes compared with reusing the same initial candidate unmodified (baseline)? The design intentionally isolates downstream interventions (validation and at‑most‑one repair) so that any paired difference is attributable to those downstream mechanisms rather than to first‑pass generation differences such as prompt engineering, constrained decoding, or sampling variance.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 1000) with deterministic task selection from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus and archived validator traces. (2) Full execution accounting: completed pairs = 1000, hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005, repair calls = 5, recorded model configuration (declared model = gpt‑5‑mini; execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset — null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). (3) Transparent confirmation that the preregistered primary test (exact two‑sided McNemar) did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625), accompanied by archived secondary descriptive summaries (paired bootstrap CI = [0.001, 0.01], bootstrap_seed = 1729) and an explicit post‑hoc labeling of any one‑sided tests as exploratory since they were not prespecified.
sections.related_work:
Empirical and survey literature documents that LLMs are prone to hallucination and prompt sensitivity that degrade correctness for generated code and configuration artifacts; these findings motivate verifier‑assisted pipelines for structured outputs [1],[2]. Constrained decoding and schema‑aware planning reduce syntactic and executable errors in several structured domains, though many demonstrations originate outside NetOps and therefore rely on validator fidelity when transferred to networking [3]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system papers emphasize verifier‑assisted repair, guarded architectures, and governance/proof‑carrying proposals to mitigate automation risks; these works present prototypes and argue that operational reliability depends on validator coverage and externally enforced protocols rather than on any single model alone [4],[5],[6].

Our study complements prior work by preregistering a paired comparison that fixes the sampled initial candidate across arms; under shared_initial_candidate semantics the experiment isolates the incremental effect of deterministic downstream validation plus a single permitted repair call, avoiding conflation with first‑pass prompt or decoding differences.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design. The study preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001) was finalized and frozen prior to any hosted‑model invocation; the preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest is ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec. Key preregistered elements: confirmatory paired binary design; task_count = 1000 deterministic tasks drawn from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per pair deterministically reused by both conditions); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. Secondary preregistered summaries: paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) and sensitivity analyses treating failed calls as unsafe.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and interpretive consequences. The archived generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate means both baseline and guarded episodes begin from the same sampled initial candidate; the guarded pipeline may reject the candidate via deterministic validation and may invoke at most one permitted repair call. Under this design, paired outcome differences can only arise from deterministic validator decisions and permitted repair(s). The design therefore does not measure effects that would arise from independent first‑pass generations, alternative prompts, or constrained decoding arms that were not executed.

Model/runtime configuration and validator. The declared provider/model is gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is explicitly not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The orchestration adapter was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5. The validator enforces workflow policies, required command presence and order, protected‑field noninterference, and returns a deterministic binary safe‑deploy verdict per task manifest.

Task corpus, selection rule, and scoring. Tasks were selected deterministically according to the preregistered ordinal rule producing 1000 unique tasks. Each task manifest includes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty labels (very_hard, extreme). Scoring used scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation producing the binary validity outcome used in the paired analysis. The preregistration specified retry and missingness rules (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1; primary analysis used 'complete_pair_primary').
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run started 2026‑09‑01T06:31:07Z and completed 2026‑09‑01T08:38:57Z. Planned episodes = 2000; completed = 2000; complete_pairs = 1000; failed episodes = 0. Provider audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005 with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5} and no cross‑condition cache reuse. All deterministic consistency checks passed.

Primary paired outcomes and preregistered confirmatory test. The 2×2 paired contingency table is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; this does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 threshold, so preregistered H1 is not supported.

Preregistered secondary descriptive summaries. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) yields [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred. All raw responses, provider call traces, repair traces (where present), and validator traces are archived in the execution manifest and analysis artifacts.
sections.discussion:
Inferential hierarchy and interpretive clarity (required revision). The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test is the study's confirmatory analysis and it did not reach two‑sided α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap CI ([0.001, 0.01]) and the one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) are reported only as preregistered descriptive summaries or explicitly labeled exploratory/post‑hoc statistics; they do not overturn the preregistered confirmatory inference. The bootstrap CI can exclude zero even when the exact test is not significant because bootstrap percentile intervals computed from resampling the observed paired outcomes are sensitive to very sparse discordant counts (here n10=5, n01=0) and can produce discrete nonzero percentile bounds; this behavior is consistent with the archived bootstrap settings (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) and the observed contingency counts.

Mechanistic interpretation. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics, only downstream validation and the permitted single repair call can alter paired outcomes. The five observed repairs illustrate that a deterministic validator with suitable coverage can correct specific ordering or protected‑field violations. The small observed absolute improvement (0.005) and the sparse discordant sample imply limited measurable marginal returns in this high‑baseline regime; the preregistered power plan had assumed a much lower baseline, so observed power to detect small absolute changes is reduced.

Threats to validity and follow‑ups. Construct validity depends on validator coverage: omitted policy checks would inflate measured success. Internal validity is strengthened by the paired shared_initial_candidate design but that design precludes measuring benefits from first‑pass generation interventions (prompt engineering, constrained decoding) that were not executed. External validity is limited by the synthetic corpus and single‑model scope. Recommended preregistered follow‑ups are: (1) independent generation arms to assess prompt/decoding interventions, (2) repair‑budget sweeps to quantify marginal returns, (3) expanded validator rule suites and topology heterogeneity, and (4) multi‑model evaluations with power calculations aligned to realistic baseline failure rates.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total model calls used = 1005. The primary inferential outcome is the preregistered exact McNemar result; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration. Artifact‑grounded evidence shows verifier‑guided repair can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflow settings, but measurable marginal gains depend on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity/coverage, and permitted repair budget. Full preregistration, execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived and available with the run to support reproducibility and preregistered follow‑ups.

limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
